children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let's begin. To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I first need to understand your situation.

**Do you have a child or children you're responsible for?** 

If yes, please tell me:
- How many children you want to check eligibility for
- Their age(s)

This will help me guide you through the right questions for your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child I'm responsible for. Alex is 8 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me work through Alex's eligibility.

Since Alex is 8 years old (under 16), that's a good start. Now I need to check a few important things.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Since Alex is 8 years old and living with you, let me continue checking the requirements.

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

(For an 8-year-old, this would typically be "yes" - they wouldn't be working full-time, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh no, Alex doesn't work at all - they're only 8! They're just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes perfect sense. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now, the next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right** (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

In other words, does Alex receive any benefits like ESA or Universal Credit in their own name? For an 8-year-old in primary school, this would typically be "no, they don't receive these benefits."

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name. They're just a regular 8-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue checking the requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Next question:

**Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?**

Again, for an 8-year-old in primary school, this would be "no" - but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - Alex is only 8 and in primary school. No apprenticeship.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Now let's move on to questions about you as the claimant.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. **Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You would qualify if ANY of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common situation)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work (up to 91 days)
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources to support your family
6. You have pre-settled status as a student with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

**Which of these applies to you?** Most people would simply answer "I normally live in the UK."

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK - I live here with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Now let me check about your responsibility for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! **Are you responsible for Alex?**

You've already mentioned that Alex lives with you at home, which meets the responsibility requirement. You would be considered responsible if ANY of these apply:

1. **You live with Alex** (which you've already confirmed)
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep (paying at least the Child Benefit amount toward their care)
3. You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

Since Alex lives with you, you meet this requirement. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now, an important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Another parent or guardian
- A former partner
- Another family member

Please let me know:
- **No one else is claiming** for Alex
- **Someone else is claiming** but you've agreed they'll transfer it to you
- **Someone else is claiming** and there's a dispute about who should claim

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's living situation. **Which of the following applies to Alex?**

- Alex is currently **in hospital**
- Alex is **in local authority care**
- Alex is **fostered**
- Alex is **living normally at home with you** (which seems to be your situation based on what you've told me)

Which one describes Alex's current situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, Alex is fostered - I'm fostering them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that! Let me check the fostering arrangement details.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Important question about the fostering arrangement:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- If the council **is NOT paying** for Alex's accommodation or maintenance, answer **YES**
- If the council **is paying** for Alex's accommodation or maintenance, answer **NO**

Foster carers can claim Child Benefit for a fostered child only if the council is not paying for the child's accommodation or maintenance. What's your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't get anything from the council for fostering Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You've confirmed the council is not paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance. Let me now get the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News - You're Eligible for Child Benefit!

Based on the information you've provided, **you ARE eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Why You're Eligible:

✅ **Alex qualifies** - Alex is 8 years old (under 16), not in paid work, not receiving benefits in their own right, and not in an apprenticeship

✅ **You meet residency requirements** - You normally live in the UK

✅ **You're responsible for Alex** - Alex lives with you as their foster carer

✅ **Special fostering rules met** - Because the local council is NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance, you can claim Child Benefit as a foster carer

✅ **No competing claims** - No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware:** If you or a partner earn over £60,000, the High Income Child Benefit Charge may apply (but you can still claim and choose not to receive payments while building National Insurance credits)
5. **Payments:** Typically made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

### How to Apply:
Visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

If you have any questions about the application process, feel free to ask!
